full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Miftah Uddin Chowdhury, J:-This rule .arises out of the Judgment and decree dated 16.07.2001, passed by the Additional District Judge, Second Court, Brahmanbaria, in Family Appeal No.15 of 2000, affirming those dated 16.07.2000, passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, War, Brahmanbaria, in Family Suit No.152 of 1998. 

 2. The short fact for disposal of the rule is that, the opposite party No. 1 Most. Ratna Begum as plaintiff instituted the suit impleading the petitioner Md. Nurul Huda Moulavi along with Md. Rafiqul Islam, Marriage Registered and another Habibur Rahman as defendant Nos.1-3 respectively for a decree for realization of dower money and maintainance and for a further declaration that the "Talakul Khula" dated 15.04.1998 is void and illegal. The plaint of the plaintiff is in brief that, she was married to (the defendant No.1) petitioner on .12.04.1997 which was registered on 02.07.1997. Moharana of the marriage was fixed at 40,000.00. The marriage was duly consummated and they gave birth of a daughter namely Amena Khatun. At the time of marriage her father presented golden ornaments worth about 12,000.00, an amount of Tk. 26,000.00 as Cash, other goods valued at Tk.15,000.00. Thereafter her husband (the defendant No.1) demandede Tk. 50,000.00 as dowry being refused he started to torture her physically and mentally. On 07.04.1998, the defendant No.1 sent her to her father's house. Therafter on 15.04,1998 she was served with a copy of talaknama. On 11.09.1998 she obtained the certified copy of the talaknama which reveals that her husband, the defendant No.1, divorced her assigning the reasons that she is mentally sick and physically unfit. Since the defendant No.1 subsequently had not been taking her care she claimed the moharana and maintenance but denied. As per the talaknama the divorce was "Talakul Khula" Hence she filed the suit for moharana, maintainance and also for declaration that the said "Talakul Khula" is illegal and void. 

 4. After hearing both the parties, the learned Assistant Judge by .his judgment and decree dated 16.07.2001 decreed the suit. declaring that the alleged "Talakul Khula" is illegal and void and the plaintiff is entitled to get Tk. 40,000.00 as her moharana and also . entitle to get Tk. 7,200:00 as her maintainance, she is entitle to get Custody of her minor daughter, and also declared that the defendant No.1 should pay Tk. 1,000.00 per month for maintainance of the daughter so long the daughter remained with .the plaintiff (mother).- On appeal preferred by the husband  (the defendant No.1) the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court was affirmed by the impugned judgment and decree dated 16.07.2001 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Second Court Brahmanbaria, in Family Appeal No.15 of 2000. 

 5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree, the husband (the defendant No.1) as 'petitioner moved this Court in revision and obtained the rule. 

 8. On query made by the. Court the petitioner Md. Nurul Huda. Moulavi, said to the Court that he 'is ready to pay the decreetal amount but not interested to live with the opposite party No.1. He prayed to the Court to allow him as custodian of their daughter Amena Begum saying that, since her age of 3 months she had been brought up by him with the help of his parents as well as his present wife. The daughter Amena Begum who is now a student of class V, on the first occasion of her presence in the Court room when her mother Ratna Begum was absent said that her mother lived in their house which means that she recognized her step mother as her own mother. On the second occasion she came to the touch of her actual mother Ratna Begum. Being invited by the actual mother she sit beside her and being asked by me whether she is interested to go with her own mother she replied that she does not know the lady (Ratna Begum). On the other occasion she shown weakness to her actual mother, but she refused to go with her. On that occasion her mother gifted her some dresses and by wearing those dresses she had been sitting in the Court room, even then she refused to go with her mother Rather by- embracing her father's neck she started crying saying "I will not leave you". Realizing her sentimental and practical situation her mother Ratna Begum admits that the daughter may be allowed to remain with her father, otherwise she will be shocked mentally. She realized the betterment of her daughter and frankly submits before the Court that she has got no objection if her daughter is allowed to remain in custody of her father. In addition; Mr. Zakaria Sarker, the learned Advocate of the petitioner submits that though the law provides the custody of minor girl in favour of the mother but for betterment of the girl the custody of- her may be determined otherwise. His such argument cannot be opposed by the learned advocate of the opposite party No.1 as well as Mrs. Ratna Begum who is a learned member of the Brahmanbaria  Bar. In prevailing circumstances, on perusal of the records hold the view that the judgment and decree passed by the Courts below so far as it relates to the amount of maharani and maintenance of the opposite party No.1 do not deserve any interference by this Court, but I hold the different view in respect of the custody of the daughter. Admittedly the daughter has been brought up by her father in his own residence since her age 3 months when the parents become separated from. each other and the father appears to be careful about the education of his daughter and even today the daughter appears happy with the company of her father. In such situation I. hold the view that the daughter Amena Begum will remain under the custody of her father as usual, but the father should allow Mst. Ratna Begum (the mother) to see her daughter on the occasions convenient to both of them and the father will also allow the mother to present any goods which will not be detrimental to the mental and physical health of the daughter and to develop her character. With the aforesaid observation, the rule is hereby discharged. Consequently, the petitioner is hereby directed to pay the rest of the decreetal amount except the amount mentioned for maintainance of the daughter-which was not paid by this time within next 3 months. Admittedly, the petitioner has already paid Tk. 24,000.00 out of the decreetal amount. Let the daughter be allowed to remain in custody of her father. And the  petitioner is hereby directed to allow the mother (Ratna Begum) to see her daughter at least once a month, he will also create to obstruction to gift anything by the-mother to her daughter which is not harmful or detrimental to her mental and physical health. The opposite party No.1 will not be entitled to get the amount as mentioned in the decree for maintenance of the daughter.
